rv.q: THE WHO'S TOMMY The Musical's timeless themes of love, alienation, and the perils of hero-worship, along with its hit songs, exciting choreography, and marvelous performances, make this rockin’ revival one worth experiencing.

The North American tour of Pete Townshend and Des McAnuff's rock opera, now playing at the Hollywood Pantages Theatre through November 15th, brings the familiar score to a visually arresting production whose theatrical ingenuity does not always translate into emotional resonance.
It is ultimately an entertaining evening if approached as a rock concert, even though the story itself is lost in the noise.
If you consider yourself a Wholigan, “The Who's TOMMY” might scratch a nostalgic itch.

cn.t: This flashy multimedia spectacle delivers raucous rock energy and visual pizzazz, but critics find it heavy on style over substance, best suited for devoted Who fans riding a wave of nostalgia.
